name_en: Complete solution to Ax = b
statement: The complete solution to Ax = b is one particular solution x_p plus any vector x_n in the nullspace: x = x_p + x_n.

anchors.quote: Please notice how I write the complete solution
Figure 3.3: Complete solution = one particular solution + all nullspace solutions.

name_en: Particular solution (free variables zero)
statement: To find one particular solution x_p to Ax = b, set all free variables to zero and solve for the pivot variables, which then come directly from d.

anchors.quote: This particular solution is my favorite: free variables = zero, pivot variables from d. The method always works.
Notice how we choose the free variables (as zero) and solve for the pivot variables.

name_en: Solvability condition for Ax = b
statement: Ax = b is solvable exactly when every zero row of R has a zero in d; equivalently b must lie in the column space of A.

anchors.quote: Ax = b and Rx = d are solvable only when all zero rows of R have zeros in d.
This is the condition to put b in the column space.

name_en: Reduce [A b] to [R d] by elimination
name_zh: 消元把 [A b] 化为 [R d]
statement: Elimination applied to the augmented matrix [A b] produces [R d]; then Ax = b has the same solutions as the simpler system Rx = d.

anchors.quote: Elimination on [A b] leads to [R d]. Then Ax = b is equivalent to Rx = d.
When we apply the usual elimination steps to A, reaching R, we also apply them to b.

name_en: Augmented matrix [A b]
statement: The augmented matrix [A b] adds the right side b as an extra column of A so that row operations act on both sides at once.

anchors.quote: One way to organize that is to add bas an extra column of the matrix.
Solution Use the augmented matrix, with its extra column b.

name_en: Full column rank (r = n)
statement: A has full column rank when r = n: all columns are pivot columns, there are no free variables, the nullspace is only the zero vector, and Ax = b has one solution or none.

anchors.quote: Every matrix A with full column rank ( r = n) has all these properties:
With full column rank, Ax = b has one solution or no solution

name_en: Full row rank (r = m)
statement: A has full row rank when r = m: every row has a pivot, the column space is all of R^m, so Ax = b has a solution for every right side b (one solution if m = n, infinitely many if m < n).

anchors.quote: Every matrix A with full row rank
2. Ax = b has a solution for every right side b.

name_en: Square invertible case r = m = n
name_zh: 方阵可逆情形 r = m = n
statement: When A is square and invertible (r = m = n), R = I has no zero rows, the nullspace is only the zero vector, and x_p = A^{-1}b is the one and only solution.

anchors.quote: Question Suppose A is a square invertible matrix,
The particular solution is the one and only solution

name_en: Four possibilities for Ax = b by rank
statement: The number of solutions to Ax = b depends on r, m, n: r = m = n gives 1 solution, r = m < n gives infinitely many, r = n < m gives 0 or 1, and r < m with r < n gives 0 or infinitely many.

anchors.quote: The four possibilities for linear equations depend on the rank r
which depend on the rank. Notice how r, m, n are the critical numbers.

name_en: Row-combination consistency for solvability
statement: If a combination of the rows of A gives the zero row, then the same combination of the entries of b must give zero; otherwise the equations are inconsistent and b is not in the column space.

anchors.quote: If a combination of the rows ( on the left side) gives the zero row, then the same combination must give zero on the right side.
If the equations are consistent, this must be true on the right side of the equations also!

name_en: Linear independence of a sequence of vectors
statement: A sequence of vectors v1,...,vn is linearly independent if the only combination x1v1+...+xnvn that gives the zero vector is the one with all x's equal to zero. Otherwise the vectors are dependent. This definition applies to any sequence of vectors in any vector space.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION The sequence of vectors $v _ { 1 } , \ldots , v _ { n }$ is linearly independent if the only combination that gives the zero vector is
Correct language: "The sequence of vectors is linearly independent." Acceptable shortcut: "The vectors are independent."

name_en: Independent columns of A
name_zh: 矩阵 A 的列无关
statement: The columns of A are linearly independent when the only solution to Ax = 0 is x = 0; no other combination Ax of the columns gives the zero vector. Equivalently the nullspace of A contains only the zero vector.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION The columns of A are linearly independent when the only solution to Ax = 0 is x = 0. No other combination Ax of the columns gives the zero vector.
The columns are independent when the nullspace $N ( A )$ contains only the zero vector.

name_en: Linear dependence
statement: Vectors are dependent when some combination with x's not all zero gives the zero vector; equivalently one vector is a combination of the other vectors. A sequence of vectors is either dependent or independent.

anchors.quote: If a combination gives 0, when the x's are not all zero, the vectors are dependent.
Note Another way to describe linear dependence is this: "One vector is a combination of the other vectors."
A sequence of vectors is either dependent or independent.

name_en: Independent columns exactly when r = n
name_zh: 列无关当且仅当秩等于 n
statement: The columns of A are independent exactly when the rank is r = n: there are n pivots and no free variables, so only x = 0 is in the nullspace. Independent columns produce full column rank.

anchors.quote: Full column rank The columns of A are independent exactly when the rank is $r = n .$ There are n pivots and no free variables.
The rank is only $r = 2$ . Independent columns produce full column rank $r = n = 3$

name_en: A matrix with m < n has dependent columns
statement: If a matrix has more columns than rows (n > m), its columns are certainly dependent: Ax = 0 has at least n - m free variables and therefore a nonzero solution. Any seven vectors from R^5 are dependent.

anchors.quote: The columns are certainly dependent if $n > m$ , because $A x = \mathbf { 0 }$ has a nonzero solution.
Then the columns must be dependent. Any seven vectors from $\mathbf { R } ^ { 5 }$ are dependent.

name_en: Spanning a space
statement: A set of vectors spans a space if their linear combinations fill the space. The columns of a matrix span its column space; they might be dependent.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION A set of vectors spans a space if their linear combinations fill the space.
The vectors $v _ { 1 } , \ldots , v _ { r }$ span a space if their combinations fill that space.
The column space is spanned by the columns.

name_en: Basis for a vector space
statement: A basis for a vector space is a sequence of vectors that are linearly independent and that span the space: not too many and not too few. A space has infinitely many different bases.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION A basis for a vector space is a sequence of vectors with two properties:
The basis vectors are linearly independent and they span the space.
Two vectors $\mathrm { c a n ' t }$ span all of $\mathbf { R } ^ { 3 }$ even if they are independent.

name_en: Unique representation in a basis
statement: Every vector v in the space is a combination of the basis vectors because they span the space, and there is one and only one such combination because the basis vectors are independent.

anchors.quote: There is one and only one way to write v as a combination of the basis vectors.
A basis consists of linearly independent vectors that span the space. Every vector in the space is a unique combination of the basis vectors.
Every vector v in the space is a combination of the basis vectors, because they span the space.

name_en: Dimension of a vector space
statement: The dimension of a space is the number of vectors in every basis for that space. It counts the degrees of freedom in the space; the dimension of R^n is n. We never speak of the rank of a space or the dimension of a basis.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION The dimension of a space is the number of vectors in every basis
The number of vectors, in any and every basis, is the "dimension" of the space.

name_en: All bases for a space have the same number of vectors
name_zh: 同一空间的所有基元素个数相同
statement: If v1,...,vm and w1,...,wn are both bases for the same vector space, then m = n. The proof assumes n > m, writes W = VA with A short and wide, and gets a nonzero solution of Ax = 0, so a combination of the w's would be zero.

anchors.quote: If $\pmb { v } _ { 1 } , \ldots , \pmb { v } _ { m }$ and $w _ { 1 } , \ldots , w _ { n }$ are both bases for the same vector space, then $m = n$
All bases for a space have the same number of vectors. This number of vectors in a basis is the dimension of the space.

name_en: Standard basis for R^n
statement: The columns of the n by n identity matrix give the standard basis for R^n: i and j in R^2, and i, j, k in R^3. They are independent and they span the space.

anchors.quote: The columns of the 3 by 3 identity matrix are the standard basis $i , j ,$ , k.
The columns of the n by n identity matrix give the "standard basis" for $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$

name_en: Row space of a matrix
statement: The row space of a matrix is the subspace of R^n spanned by its rows: all combinations of the rows. It is the column space of A transpose, and it is a subspace of R^n while the column space lives in R^m.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION The row space of a matrix is the subspace of $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$ spanned by the rows.
The columns span the column space. Here is a new subspace-which is spanned by the rows.
The row space contains all combinations of the rows. This row space of A is the column space of $A ^ { \mathrm { T } }$

name_en: C(A^T) for the row space
statement: The row space of A is written C(A^T), the column space of A transpose: transposing turns the rows of A into columns, so the same numbers now span a subspace of R^n. The left nullspace is written N(A^T).

anchors.quote: The row space of A is $C ( A ^ { \mathrm { T } } )$ . It is the column space of
Instead of the rows of A, look at the columns of $A ^ { \mathrm { T } }$ . Same numbers, but now in the column space

name_en: Columns of an invertible matrix are a basis for R^n
name_zh: 可逆矩阵的列构成 R^n 的基
statement: The vectors v1,...,vn are a basis for R^n exactly when they are the columns of an n by n invertible matrix. Then Ax = 0 forces x = 0 (independence) and Ax = b is always solvable by x = A^{-1}b (spanning), so R^n has infinitely many different bases.

anchors.quote: The vectors $v _ { 1 } , \ldots , v _ { n }$ are a basis for $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$ exactly when they are the columns of an n by n invertible matrix.
The columns of every invertible n by n matrix give a basis for $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$
The only solution to $A x = \mathbf { 0 }$ is $\pmb { x } = \pmb { A } ^ { - 1 } \mathbf { 0 } = \mathbf { 0 }$ . The columns are independent.

name_en: Finding a basis by elimination
statement: To find a basis for the space spanned by given vectors: either make them the rows of A and eliminate, keeping the nonzero rows of R, or put them in the columns of A and eliminate, keeping the pivot columns of A (not of R).

anchors.quote: Question Given five vectors in ${ \bf R } ^ { 7 }$ , how do you find a basis for the space they span?
First answer Make them the rows of A, and eliminate to find the nonzero rows of R.
Eliminate to find the pivot columns (of A not R). Those pivot columns are a basis for the column space.

name_en: Bases for matrix spaces and function spaces
name_zh: 矩阵空间与函数空间的基
statement: Independence, basis and dimension are not restricted to column vectors. The space of all 2 by 2 matrices has dimension 4 and the n by n matrix space has dimension n^2; the solution space of y'' = -y has the two basis functions sin x and cos x, so its dimension is 2.

anchors.quote: The words "independence" and "basis" and "dimension" are not at all restricted to column vectors.
Matrix spaces The vector space M contains all 2 by 2 matrices. Its dimension is 4.
That solution space for $y ^ { \prime \prime } = - y$ has two basis functions: sin x and cos x.

name_en: The four fundamental subspaces
statement: The four fundamental subspaces of an m by n matrix are the row space C(A^T) and nullspace N(A) in R^n, and the column space C(A) and left nullspace N(A^T) in R^m. Two come directly from A and two from A transpose; the rank of A reveals all four dimensions.

anchors.quote: Four Fundamental Subspaces 1. The row space is $C(A^{\mathrm{T}})$, a subspace of $\mathbf{R}^{n}$. 2. The column space is $C(A)$, a subspace of $\mathbf{R}^{m}$.
4. The left nullspace is $N(A^{\mathrm{T}})$, a subspace of $\mathbf{R}^{m}$. This is our new space.
The rank of A reveals the dimensions of all four fundamental subspaces.

name_en: Left nullspace N(A^T)
statement: The left nullspace of A is the nullspace of A transpose: the solutions y of A^T y = 0, a subspace of R^m. Written y^T A = 0^T the vectors y sit on the left of A and combine the rows of A to give the zero row.

anchors.quote: 4. The left nullspace is $N(A^{\mathrm{T}})$, a subspace of $\mathbf{R}^{m}$.
The vectors y go on the $l e f t$ side of A when the equation is written
The y's in the left nulspace combine the rows to give the zero row.

name_en: Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra, Part 1
name_zh: 线性代数基本定理第一部分
statement: For an m by n matrix of rank r: the column space and row space both have dimension r, the nullspace has dimension n - r and the left nullspace has dimension m - r. The rank of A therefore fixes the dimensions of all four fundamental subspaces.

anchors.quote: Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra, Part 1
The column space and row space both have dimension r.
The nullspaces have dimensions n - r and m - r.

name_en: Rank Theorem: column rank equals row rank
statement: The number of independent columns equals the number of independent rows: the column space of A has dimension r, the same as the row space. The right reason is that the same combinations of columns are zero for A and for R, since Ax = 0 exactly when Rx = 0.

anchors.quote: Rank Theorem: The number of independent columns =the number of independent rows
2 The column space of A has dimension r. The column rank equals the row rank.

name_en: Counting Theorem: r + (n - r) = n
statement: There are n - r free variables, so the dimension of the nullspace is n - r: (dimension of column space) + (dimension of nullspace) = dimension of R^n. The counting rule for A^T is r + (m - r) = m.

anchors.quote: There are $n - r$ free variables, so the dimension of the nullspace is $n - r$ . This is the Counting Theorem
( dimension of column space) + ( dimension of nullspace) = dimension of $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$
The counting rule for A was $r + ( n - r ) = n$

name_en: The n - r special solutions are a basis for the nullspace
name_zh: n-r 个特解构成零空间的基
statement: There is one special solution for each free variable, so with n variables and r pivots there are n - r of them. They are independent because they contain the identity matrix in the free rows, so they form a basis for the nullspace, which has dimension n - r.

anchors.quote: The nullspace has dimension $n - r$ . The special solutions form a basis
Reason: There is a special solution for each free variable.
The next section shows that the $n - r$ special solutions always give a basis for the nullspace.

name_en: Elimination changes rows but not the row space or nullspace
name_zh: 消元不改变行空间与零空间
statement: A has the same row space as R and the same nullspace as R, with the same dimensions and the same bases, because every row of A is a combination of the rows of R and conversely, and the elimination steps do not change the solutions of Ax = 0.

anchors.quote: 1 A has the same row space as R. Same dimension rand same basis.
Reason: Every row of A is a combination of the rows of R. Also every row of R is a combination of the rows of A. Elimination changes rows, but not row spaces.
3 A has the same nullspace as R Same dimension $n - r$ and same basis

name_en: The r pivot columns of A are a basis for C(A)
name_zh: A 的 r 个主元列构成列空间的基
statement: The pivot columns of A are a basis for its column space: they are independent because they start with the r by r identity matrix, and every free column is a combination of them. The dimension of the column space is r. Note that the pivot columns of A must be used, not those of R.

anchors.quote: Conclusion The r pivot columns of A are a basis for its column space $C ( A )$
The pivot columns are independent, and they span, so they are a basis for C(R).
The pivot columns of A are a basis for its column space.

name_en: The r pivot rows are a basis for the row space
name_zh: r 个主元行构成行空间的基
statement: The r pivot rows of R are a basis for the row space of R and of A (the same space): the nonzero rows of R are independent because in the pivot columns they contain the r by r identity matrix, and they span the row space. The dimension of the row space is r.

anchors.quote: 1. The r pivot rows of Rare a basis for the row spaces of Rand A (same space).
So the r pivot rows are a basis for the row space.
The pivot rows of A are a basis for its row space. So are the pivot rows of its echelon form R.

name_en: Rank one matrix A = uv^T
statement: Every rank one matrix is one column times one row, A = uv^T: every row is a multiple of v^T, which is a basis for the one-dimensional row space, and every column is a multiple of u, which is a basis for the column space.

anchors.quote: Every rank one matrix is one column times one row $A = u v ^ { \mathrm { T } }$
On the left is a matrix with three rows. But its row space only has dimension $= ~ 1$
"The column rank equals the row rank which is l."

name_en: Orthogonal vectors
statement: Two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero. The test is v^T w = 0.

anchors.quote: Two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero

name_en: Pythagorean law for orthogonal vectors
statement: For orthogonal vectors v and w (v^T w = 0), the squared lengths add: ||v||^2 + ||w||^2 = ||v + w||^2. This is the right-triangle relation a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

anchors.quote: for a right triangle with sides v and w
\| \boldsymbol {v} \| ^ {2} + \| \boldsymbol {w} \| ^ {2} = \| \boldsymbol {v} + \boldsymbol {w} \| ^ {2}.

name_en: Orthogonal subspaces
statement: Two subspaces V and W are orthogonal if every vector v in V is perpendicular to every vector w in W, i.e. v^T w = 0 for all such pairs.

anchors.quote: Two subspaces V and $W$ of a vector space are orthogonal if every vector v in V is perpendicular to every vector w in $W$
Subspaces V and Ware orthogonal if every v in Vis orthogonal to every win W.

name_en: Row space is orthogonal to the nullspace
statement: The row space C(A^T) and the nullspace N(A) are orthogonal subspaces of R^n. Every row of A is perpendicular to every solution of Ax = 0.

anchors.quote: The row space is perpendicular to the nullspace. Every row of A is perpendicular to every solution of
The nulspace $N ( A )$ and the row space $C ( A ^ { \mathrm { T } } )$ are orthogonal subspaces of

name_en: Column space is orthogonal to the left nullspace
name_zh: 列空间与左零空间正交
statement: The column space C(A) and the left nullspace N(A^T) are always orthogonal subspaces of R^m. Every vector in N(A^T) is perpendicular to every column of A.

anchors.quote: The column space of A and the nullspace of $\dot { \boldsymbol { A } } ^ { \mathrm { T } }$ are always orthogonal subspaces.
The left nullspace $N ( A ^ { \mathrm { T } } )$ and the column space $C ( A )$ are orthogonal in

name_en: Only the zero vector lies in two orthogonal subspaces
name_zh: 两个正交子空间只共有零向量
statement: When a vector is in two orthogonal subspaces it must be zero, since it is perpendicular to itself. A vector orthogonal to itself is the zero vector.

anchors.quote: When a vector is in two orthogonal subspaces, it must be zero. It is perpendicular to itself.
If a vector v is orthogonal to itself then v is the zero vector.

name_en: Orthogonal complement
statement: The orthogonal complement of a subspace V contains every vector perpendicular to V. The nullspace complement N(A)^perp is exactly the row space C(A^T).

anchors.quote: The orthogonal complement of a subspace V contains every vector that is perpendicular to V
We conclude that the nullspace complement $N ( A ) ^ { \perp }$ is exactly the row space

name_en: Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra, Part 2
name_zh: 线性代数基本定理第二部分
statement: N(A) is the orthogonal complement of the row space C(A^T) in R^n, and N(A^T) is the orthogonal complement of the column space C(A) in R^m. This is the perpendicularity of the four subspaces.
aliases: Part 2 of the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra

anchors.quote: This perpendicularity of subspaces is Part 2 of the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra.
$N ( A )$ is the orthogonal complement of the row space $C ( A ^ { \mathrm { T } } )$

name_en: Splitting a vector into row-space and nullspace components
name_zh: 向量分解为行空间与零空间分量
statement: Because the row space and nullspace are orthogonal complements, every x in R^n splits uniquely as x = x_r + x_n, a row space component plus a nullspace component.

anchors.quote: every x can be split into a row space component
Each x is the sum $x _ { r } + x _ { n }$ of a row space vector

name_en: A is invertible from row space to column space
name_zh: A 在行空间到列空间上可逆
statement: Every vector b in the column space comes from one and only one vector x_r in the row space. From the row space to the column space, A acts as an invertible (r by r) map.

anchors.quote: Every vector b in the column space comes from one and only one vector
From the row space to the column space, $A$ is invertible.

name_en: Orthogonal complement notation V perp
statement: The orthogonal complement of a subspace V is denoted V^perp, pronounced "V perp".

anchors.quote: This orthogonal subspace is denoted by $V ^ { \perp }$ (pronounced "V perp").

name_en: Dot product written as v^T w
statement: The dot product of v and w is written v . w = v^T w, so the orthogonality condition is v^T w = 0.

anchors.quote: their dot product is zero: $\boldsymbol { v } \boldsymbol { \cdot w } = \boldsymbol { v } ^ { \mathrm { T } } \boldsymbol { w } = \boldsymbol { 0 }$
$v ^ { \mathrm { T } } w = 0$ for all v in V and all w in W.

name_en: projection of a vector onto a line
name_zh: 向量在一条直线上的投影
statement: The projection of b onto the line through a is its closest point p, the part of b along that line. It is found in three steps: find the number x-hat, then the vector p, then the matrix P.

anchors.quote: When b is projected onto a line, its projection pis the part of b along that line
These three steps will lead to all projection matrices: find ${ \widehat { \mathbf { x } } } ,$ , then find the vector

name_en: the coefficient x-hat
statement: x-hat ("x hat") denotes the best coefficient giving the closest vector in the subspace. For a line, x-hat = a^T b / a^T a.

anchors.quote: The hat over x indicates the best choice x, to give the closest vector in the column space.
Our formula ${ \widehat { \pmb x } } = { \pmb a } ^ { \mathrm { T } } { \pmb b } / { \pmb a } ^ { \mathrm { T } } { \pmb a }$ gives the projection

name_en: projection formula p = (a^T b / a^T a) a
name_zh: 直线投影公式 p = (a^T b / a^T a) a
statement: The projection of b onto the line through a is the vector p = x-hat a = (a^T b / a^T a) a.

anchors.quote: The projection of b onto the line through a is the vector
The projection of b onto the line through a is $\pmb { p } = \pmb { a } \widehat { \pmb { x } } = \pmb { a } ( \pmb { a } ^ { \mathrm { T } } \pmb { b } / a ^ { \mathrm { T } } \pmb { a } )$

name_en: error vector e = b - p
name_zh: 误差向量 e = b - p
statement: The error vector is e = b - p, the difference between b and its projection p. The vectors p and e add to b.

anchors.quote: The error vector between $^ { b }$ and $_ p$ is $e = b - p$ .
The dotted line $b - p$ is the "error" $e = b - { \widehat { x } } a$

name_en: error is perpendicular to the line
statement: The error e = b - p is perpendicular to a. The right triangle b, p, e satisfies ||p||^2 + ||e||^2 = ||b||^2.

anchors.quote: The error $e = \pmb { b } - \pmb { p }$ is perpendicular to a: Right triangle b p e has
The error e should be perpendicular to

name_en: rank-one projection matrix P = a a^T / a^T a
name_zh: 秩一投影矩阵 P = a a^T / a^T a
statement: The projection matrix onto the line through a is P = a a^T / a^T a: a column times a row divided by the number a^T a. P is m by m but has rank one.

anchors.quote: The projection matrix $P$ is $m$ by $m ,$ , but its rank is one.
The rank one projection matrix $P = { { a } { { a } ^ { \mathrm { T } } } / { { a } ^ { \mathrm { T } } } }$ a multiplies b to produce $p .$

name_en: projection matrix
statement: A projection matrix P is a symmetric matrix with P^2 = P; it multiplies b to give its projection p = Pb.

anchors.quote: The projection matrix P multiplies b to give p. This section finds p and also P.
symmetric matrices with $P ^ { 2 } = P$ . The projection of bis Pb.

name_en: projection of a vector onto a subspace
name_zh: 向量在子空间上的投影
statement: Projecting b onto the subspace spanned by independent columns of A (its column space): find the closest combination p by the same three steps, find x-hat, then p = A x-hat, then P.

anchors.quote: The projection of b onto a subspace Sis the closest vector pin
We compute projections onto n-dimensional subspaces in three steps as before

name_en: the equation A^T A x-hat = A^T b
name_zh: 法方程 A^T A x-hat = A^T b
statement: The equation for the best x-hat is A^T A x-hat = A^T b, the "famous form" of A^T(b - A x-hat) = 0 with coefficient matrix A^T A.

anchors.quote: in its famous form $A ^ { \mathrm { T } } A { \widehat { \mathbf { x } } } = A ^ { \mathrm { T } } b$
Now solve the normal equation $A ^ { \mathrm { T } } A { \widehat { \mathbf { x } } } = A ^ { \mathrm { T } } t$ to find x:

name_en: projection formula p = A (A^T A)^{-1} A^T b
name_zh: 子空间投影公式 p = A (A^T A)^{-1} A^T b
statement: The projection of b onto the column space of A is the vector p = A (A^T A)^{-1} A^T b.

anchors.quote: Then the projection of b onto the column space of A is the vector
The projection of b onto the subspace is p:

name_en: projection matrix P = A (A^T A)^{-1} A^T
name_zh: 列空间投影矩阵 P = A (A^T A)^{-1} A^T
statement: The projection matrix onto the column space C(A) is P = A (A^T A)^{-1} A^T; it satisfies p = Pb.

anchors.quote: The projection matrix is $P = A ( A ^ { \mathrm { T } } A ) ^ { - 1 } A ^ { \mathrm { T } }$
The projection matrix $\overset { \cdot } { P } = \overset { \cdot } { A } ( A ^ { \mathrm { T } } A ) ^ { - 1 } A ^ { \mathrm { T } }$ gives $p = P b$

name_en: projection matrix is symmetric and idempotent
statement: The projection matrix satisfies P^T = P and P^2 = P: projecting a second time does not change the result.

anchors.quote: has $P ^ { \mathrm { T } } = P$ and $P ^ { 2 } = P$ and $P b = p$
Projecting a second time doesn't change anything, so $P ^ { 2 } = P$

name_en: A^T A is invertible iff A has independent columns
name_zh: A^T A 可逆当且仅当 A 的列线性无关
statement: A^T A is invertible if and only if A has linearly independent columns; A^T A has the same nullspace as A, and when A has independent columns A^T A is square, symmetric, and invertible.

anchors.quote: A is invertible if and only if A has linearly independent columns.
When A has independent columns, $A ^ { \mathrm { T } } A$ is square, symmetric, and invertible.

name_en: error is orthogonal to the subspace / in N(A^T)
name_zh: 误差与子空间正交 / 在 A^T 的零空间中
statement: The error vector b - A x-hat is perpendicular to the column space of A, hence lies in the nullspace of A^T (the left nullspace).

anchors.quote: The error vector $\pmb { b } - A \widehat { \pmb { x } }$ is perpendicular to that column space.
That nullspace of $A ^ { \mathrm { T } }$ contains the error vector $e = \pmb { b } - A \widehat { \pmb { x } }$ .
